newsitem.title: UK: Industry oil stockdraw just 0.1 mln bpd in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Industry oil stockdraw just 0.1 mln bpd in Q1.

text.p: Mild weather and growing oil supplies have left stocks of oil held by industry barely dented in the critical winter months this year, according to the Paris-based International Energy Agency (IEA).

They were drawn down by just 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) in the first quarter this year compared to 1.5 million bpd in 1996, the IEA said in its latest Monthly Oil Market Report published on Tuesday.
Oil stocks held by industry, rather than by governments, are typically drawn down fastest in the cold winter months.
In the two previous years the draw on stocks was 1.3 million bpd (1Q95) and 1.4 million bpd (1Q94), giving an average draw of 1.4 million bpd in the previous three years.
The IEA said mild weather and strong supply growth in the first quarter this year resulted in an abnormally small stockdraw.
In North America total oil stocks were above previous year levels for the first time since June 1995.

Full details of how stocks were drawn in March are not yet available but the IEA said a lower than expected draw in February of just 500,000 bpd left total stocks appreciably higher than the levels of last year.
In the U.S. gasoline stocks remained at a low level and in Europe crude oil stocks fell but remained above average for end of February levels.
European middle distillate stocks showed a contraseasonal increase of 300,000 bpd and there were unusually small stockdraws of 200,000 bpd in the North American and the Pacific regions.
Due to a big upward revision of European stock levels in January, the stock change during that month was switched to a stockbuild of 700,000 bpd from a small stock draw, the IEA said.
This meant total stocks in the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) were well above 1996 levels for the first two months of this year.
The year-on-year difference reached more than 100 million barrels in February, spread across all regions with Europe accounting for more than half the difference.
Middle distillates showed the biggest gains although stocks were also higher for crude oil and fuel oil.
Gasoline stocks in Europe and the United States were well below previous years levels.
At the end of February industry stocks covered 58 days of forward demand, or one day more than at the same time last year.
In North America, total oil stocks were above previous year levels for the first time since June 1995.
This was mainly due to the smaller than normal stockdraw of 100,000 bpd in February.

In Europe, industry stocks fell 100,000 bpd in February, albeit from upwardly revised January levels. The biggest January revision was for crude oil stock levels, which reached their highest level since July 1996.
Crude oil stocks were drawn by 500,000 bpd in February as refinery runs rose but they remain well above the average end of February level for the past five years.
Despite gasoline stocks staying almost unchanged in February they ended February 5 million barrels below last year's level.
Mainly due to mild weather middle distillate stocks showed a contraseasonal rise of 300,000 bpd with big increases in Germany, France and the Netherlands.
In the Pacific, total oil stocks were drawn by 200,000 bpd a much smaller fall than the average over the past five years.
Crude oil stocks stayed almost unchanged from end of January levels while gasoline and fuel rose slightly to typical levels for the time of year.
Middle distillates continued their seasonal decline but remained 10 million barrels above last years level.
-- London newsroom, 44 171 542 4984
